newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Michelin picks up RSS3 in Singapore rubber market.
newsitem.headline: Michelin picks up RSS3 in Singapore rubber market.

text.p: Michelin was said to have bought some nearby RSS3 rubber as part of its regular buying programme on Wednesday while news of large stocks in Thailand continued to weigh on the market, dealers said.

"Michelin was in for some RSS3. But this is just part of their regular buying during a week," a dealer said. Another dealer said Bridgestone, which bought some TSR20 rubber yesterday, was also probably in the market.
Goodyear was not seen in the market today in an otherwise lacklustre session in the local exchange.
Traders said news that an industry official said Thailand has excess stocks of up to 140,000 tonnes continued to exert a bearish hold on the market.

"It's still having a major impact," a dealer said, adding though that other factors kept people sidelined such as the mostly weakly performance of Tokyo, where benchmark January was down one yen at 119.1.
At 0945 GMT, September RSS3 was seen unchanged at 94.00 U.S. cents a kg. September RSS1 was seen at 137.25 Singapore cents (93 U.S. cents) a kg from 137.00 cents.
